references.rationale: Links the chromestatus entry, CSSWG issue #12953 and the feature index.

conformance.rationale: Feature suite reads the exact dictionary member via ordered getters, checks sequence<ShadowRoot> TypeErrors, and asserts real capture/non-capture and duplicate rejection on an element-scoped transition; 7 of 8 fail on Chromium 157, so every positive probe can fail.

telemetry_health.rationale: Asserts probe tier on load and that the captured names match the tier after each primary action; superseded AbortErrors are not reported as failures.

design_system.rationale: Only design-system variables for text/background; button colour overrides set both background and color; accent-blue on ivory/stone is well above AA.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Driven at 1280x800 and 360x740 DPR3 touch: no horizontal overflow, controls >= 44px, readouts wrap; screenshots read for both classes.

spec_match.rationale: Compares the ::part() workaround named in the issue with the option, and exercises sequence<ShadowRoot> conversion errors, closed-root encapsulation and the shared-namespace duplicate rule from the Chromium implementation.

interactive.rationale: Strategy radios + run, two duplicate-name calls, and four invalid/closed-root calls each make a real element-scoped startViewTransition() call and print the outcome.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index blurb lists workaround, duplicate skip, TypeError cases and closed roots; all on the page.

edge_cases.rationale: This is the edge/migration concept: covers ignoring browsers, conversion-time TypeError (no DOM update), ready rejection with DOM still updated, and the owner-only closed-root path.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 157 headless: ::part() strategy captured chip-via-part, the option strategy captured nothing extra, the duplicate never collided and invalid entries ran without throwing — all labelled as the ignoring-browser branch; console clean. TypeError/InvalidStateError branches unexecuted here (InvalidStateError mechanism positively controlled with a light-DOM duplicate).

accessibility.rationale: Fieldset/legend radios, native 44px buttons with the exact call as their label, one polite readout per panel.

openQuestions.title: Capture the supported path on a Chromium build with ViewTransitionShadowRoots
openQuestions.detail: The flag landed in Chromium main in Nov 2026; neither Chrome for Testing 153 nor Chromium 157 in the verification container has it (the getter probe returns 'ignored' even with --enable-blink-features=ViewTransitionShadowRoots). Re-run this page on Canary/M160 with the flag and confirm the shadow-tree names appear in the readout and the telemetry assert passes on the supported branch.

openQuestions.title: Re-check against the spec text once CSSWG edits land
openQuestions.detail: The chromestatus spec anchor #dom-startviewtransitionoptions-shadowroots does not exist in the published draft yet (issue #12953 is labelled Needs Edits). Participation rules here follow the resolution and Chromium's view_transition_style_tracker.cc; confirm against normative text when published, especially duplicate-name and nested-root behaviour.

openQuestions.title: Inspect the accessibility tree with chrome-devtools-mcp
openQuestions.detail: Verification used headless Chromium via Playwright (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this environment); names/roles were checked from DOM only (project rule 7b).

guidanceConsulted.query: view transitions in web components shadow DOM
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use document.startViewTransition with view-transition-name on persisting elements and await transition.ready before reading pseudo-element state.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Capture is read only after transition.ready resolves, from document.getAnimations() on the ::view-transition-* pseudo-elements; ready rejections are caught and superseded-transition AbortErrors ignored.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Respect reduced motion case by case; only dampen spatial movement and keep non-motion transitions.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce the group (spatial morph) animation-name is set to none; the opacity cross-fade on old/new stays, which also keeps the capture readout working. Exception to scoped-component-transitions' 'animation: none !important on old/new' because that would remove the only observable of capture; the remaining fade is non-spatial.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive layout without horizontal overflow on mobile
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use intrinsic/flexible layouts and min-inline-size:0 so content fits narrow viewports.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Flex-wrap control rows, min-inline-size:0 panels, pre-wrap/overflow-wrap:anywhere readouts; scrollWidth === innerWidth at 360x740 DPR3.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible toggle buttons aria-pressed segmented control
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use native controls with labels, 44px targets, visible focus and polite live regions for state changes.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Native checkboxes/radios inside labels and fieldsets, native buttons at min-height 44px, a single role=status aria-live=polite readout per demo.

guidanceConsulted.query: view transitions in web components shadow DOM
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Cross the shadow boundary deliberately: custom properties for theming, ::part for exported internals; avoid :host-context.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Shadow styles read design-system custom properties (var(--accent-blue) etc.) that inherit across the boundary; ::part is shown only as the legacy workaround being migrated away from.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Call startViewTransition on the component root, catch transition.ready, and feature-detect on Element.prototype with an instant-update fallback.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Element-scoped transitions run on the component/lane; 'startViewTransition' in Element.prototype gates an instant update fallback; ready.catch attached.

summary: Migration and failure modes, each a real call. On Chromium 157 every option-dependent branch is honestly reported as ignored while the ::part() workaround is shown working. TypeError and duplicate-rejection branches await a supporting build.
